title: Alcohols and Carboxylic Acids – Homologous Series and Properties
topic: Alcohols (C1–C4) and Carboxylic Acids (C1–C4), Oxidation, and Acid Reactions
subject: Combined Science Chemistry
description: This worksheet covers the first four members of the alcohol and carboxylic acid homologous series. You will need to identify structures and formulas, understand oxidation of alcohols using acidified KMnO₄, and predict reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, carbonates, and bases.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of the third member of the alcohol homologous series?
questions.explanation: The third member of the alcohol series is propanol (C₃H₇OH). The first is methanol (CH₃OH), the second is ethanol (C₂H₅OH).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct general formula for the homologous series of alcohols with a single hydroxyl group?
questions.explanation: The general formula for saturated alcohols is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where n = 1, 2, 3, ...

questions.question: What is the name of the carboxylic acid with the molecular formula C₃H₇COOH?
questions.explanation: The general formula for carboxylic acids is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH. For C₃H₇COOH, n = 4, which corresponds to butanoic acid.

questions.question: A compound has the structure CH₃CH₂CH₂OH. Which homologous series does it belong to, and what is its name?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH is the structure for propanol. It has three carbon atoms in the chain with the OH group at the end.

questions.question: What is the functional group present in all carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: All carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl functional group, which is written as –COOH.

questions.question: Which reagent is used to oxidise a primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid in the laboratory?
questions.explanation: Acidified potassium manganate(VII) (KMnO₄) is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises primary alcohols to carboxylic acids. The purple solution turns colourless.

questions.question: A primary alcohol with the formula C₂H₅OH is oxidised using acidified KMnO₄. What is the name of the organic product formed?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is oxidised to ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) when reacted with acidified KMnO₄.

questions.question: Which of the following alcohols can be oxidised to a carboxylic acid using acidified KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: Primary alcohols (where the –OH is on a terminal carbon) can be oxidised to carboxylic acids. Propanol is a primary alcohol; secondary alcohols do not oxidise to carboxylic acids.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium metal. Which of the following is a product of this reaction?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with reactive metals like magnesium to produce a salt and hydrogen gas. 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂.

questions.question: Propanoic acid is added to sodium carbonate solution. What gas is produced?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to produce a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas. 2C₂H₅COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2C₂H₅COONa + H₂O + CO₂.

questions.question: Methanoic acid is neutralised by sodium hydroxide solution. What is the name of the salt produced?
questions.explanation: When methanoic acid (HCOOH) reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH), the salt formed is sodium methanoate (HCOONa).

questions.question: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid. Which statement about ethanoic acid is correct?
options: It is fully ionised in aqueous solution
It reacts with sodium carbonate to produce hydrogen gas
It is a strong acid with a pH of 1
It only partially ionises in aqueous solution
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, meaning it only partially ionises in water to produce hydrogen ions.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of butanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Butanoic acid has four carbon atoms in the chain, so its molecular formula is C₃H₇COOH (or C₄H₈O₂).

questions.question: A student adds a few drops of acidified KMnO₄ to a sample of propanol and warms the mixture. The purple colour disappears. What product is formed?
questions.explanation: Propanol is a primary alcohol. Acidified KMnO₄ oxidises it to propanoic acid.

questions.question: A compound has the molecular formula C₃H₇OH. What is the name of this alcohol?
questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH corresponds to propanol, the third member of the alcohol homologous series.

questions.question: When butanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate, the products are sodium butanoate, water, and one other substance. What is this other substance?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to produce a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas.

questions.question: A compound has the functional group –COOH. It reacts with magnesium to produce hydrogen gas. Which homologous series does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The –COOH group is the carboxyl group found in carboxylic acids. They react with reactive metals to produce hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which of the following alcohols will NOT undergo oxidation to a carboxylic acid when treated with acidified KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol (the –OH is on the middle carbon). Oxidation of secondary alcohols produces ketones, not carboxylic acids. Primary alcohols oxidise to carboxylic acids.

questions.question: A student tests a colourless liquid with litmus paper. The paper turns red. A small piece of magnesium is added, and bubbles of gas are observed. The gas burns with a squeaky pop. What is the liquid most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid turns litmus red (acidic) and reacts with magnesium to produce hydrogen gas (squeaky pop). Ethanol is neutral and does not react with magnesium.

questions.question: What is the name of the salt formed when propanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explanation: The salt formed from propanoic acid (C₂H₅COOH) and sodium hydroxide is sodium propanoate (C₂H₅COONa).
